description: An introduction to magnets and magnetic fields, the magnetic effect of an electric current, electromagnets and their applications, the motor effect, electromagnetic induction, and the simple electric motor and generator.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following materials is attracted to a magnet?
mcq.explanation: Iron is a ferromagnetic material and is strongly attracted to magnets, while copper, aluminium and wood are non-magnetic.

mcq.questionText: When two like poles of magnets are brought close together, they will:
mcq.explanation: The law of magnetism states that like poles repel while unlike poles attract.

mcq.questionText: The region around a magnet where its magnetic force can be detected is called the:
mcq.explanation: A magnetic field is the space around a magnet within which a magnetic force acts on magnetic materials.

mcq.questionText: Outside a bar magnet, magnetic field lines are drawn pointing from the:

options.text: South pole to the north pole
North pole to the south pole

mcq.explanation: By convention, magnetic field lines outside a magnet travel from the north pole to the south pole.

mcq.questionText: Which instrument uses a small magnetised needle to show direction by aligning with the Earth's magnetic field?
mcq.explanation: A magnetic compass has a freely pivoting magnetised needle that aligns itself with the Earth's magnetic field.

mcq.questionText: The experiment in which a compass needle moves when placed near a current-carrying wire demonstrates that:

options.text: An electric current produces a magnetic field
A magnet produces an electric current
Heat is produced by the wire
The wire becomes a permanent magnet

mcq.explanation: Oersted's discovery showed that an electric current flowing through a conductor produces a magnetic field around it.

mcq.questionText: An electromagnet is best described as a magnet that:

options.text: Is magnetic only while current flows through its coil
Is made from a piece of steel

mcq.explanation: An electromagnet is a temporary magnet that is magnetic only while an electric current flows through its coil.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following will increase the strength of an electromagnet?

options.text: Decreasing the current in the coil
Reducing the number of turns of wire
Increasing the number of turns of wire

mcq.explanation: Increasing the number of turns of the coil increases the strength of an electromagnet, as does increasing the current and using a soft-iron core.

mcq.questionText: The core of a strong electromagnet is usually made from:
mcq.explanation: Soft iron is used because it magnetises strongly and loses its magnetism quickly when the current is switched off.

mcq.questionText: In an electric bell, the device that repeatedly attracts the armature to make the hammer strike the gong is the:
mcq.explanation: The electromagnet in an electric bell attracts the soft-iron armature, and the make-and-break contact causes it to vibrate and ring the gong.

mcq.questionText: A relay is a device that uses a small current to:

options.text: Switch on or off a separate larger circuit

mcq.explanation: A relay uses an electromagnet operated by a small current to open or close the contacts of a separate, often larger, circuit.

mcq.questionText: The turning effect produced when a current-carrying conductor is placed in a magnetic field is called the:
mcq.explanation: The motor effect is the force experienced by a current-carrying conductor placed in a magnetic field.

mcq.questionText: Producing an electric current by moving a magnet near a coil of wire is known as:
mcq.explanation: Electromagnetic induction is the production of a voltage (and current) in a conductor due to a changing magnetic field.

mcq.questionText: A device that converts electrical energy into mechanical (rotational) energy is the:
mcq.explanation: An electric motor uses the motor effect to convert electrical energy into mechanical energy of rotation.

mcq.questionText: A simple generator works on the principle of:
mcq.explanation: A generator rotates a coil in a magnetic field, inducing a current by electromagnetic induction, converting mechanical energy into electrical energy.

fib.questionText: A magnet has two poles called the north pole and the _____ pole.
fib.explanation: Every magnet has two poles: a north-seeking pole and a south-seeking pole.

fib.questionText: Unlike magnetic poles attract while like poles _____ each other.
fib.explanation: This is the basic law of magnetism governing the interaction between magnetic poles.

fib.questionText: The pattern of a magnetic field can be shown using iron _____ sprinkled on paper over a magnet.
fib.explanation: Iron filings line up along the magnetic field lines, revealing the shape of the field.

fib.questionText: The scientist who discovered that an electric current produces a magnetic field was _____.
fib.explanation: Hans Christian Oersted observed a compass needle deflect near a current-carrying wire.

fib.questionText: A coil of wire wound into many turns, used to produce a magnetic field, is called a _____.
fib.explanation: A solenoid is a long coil of wire that behaves like a bar magnet when carrying current.

fib.questionText: The strength of an electromagnet increases when the _____ flowing through the coil is increased.
fib.explanation: Larger current, more turns and a soft-iron core all increase electromagnet strength.

fib.questionText: In a moving-coil _____, sound is produced when a current in a coil interacts with a permanent magnet to move a cone.
fib.explanation: A loudspeaker uses the motor effect on a coil to vibrate a cone and produce sound waves.

fib.questionText: The _____ effect describes the force on a current-carrying wire placed in a magnetic field.
fib.explanation: This force is the principle behind the operation of electric motors.

fib.questionText: When a magnet is moved in or out of a coil, a voltage is _____ in the coil.
fib.explanation: A changing magnetic field through a coil induces a voltage by electromagnetic induction.

fib.questionText: A device that converts mechanical energy into electrical energy is called a _____.
fib.explanation: A generator uses electromagnetic induction to produce electricity from rotational motion.

tf.questionText: A magnet has its strongest pulling force at its poles.
tf.explanation: The magnetic force is concentrated and strongest at the two poles of a magnet.

tf.questionText: Steel is used to make permanent magnets because it keeps its magnetism for a long time.
tf.explanation: Steel retains magnetism well, making it suitable for permanent magnets, unlike soft iron.

tf.questionText: Two unlike magnetic poles repel each other.
tf.explanation: Unlike poles attract each other; it is like poles that repel.

tf.questionText: An electromagnet loses most of its magnetism when the current is switched off.
tf.explanation: Because it uses a soft-iron core, an electromagnet is a temporary magnet that loses its magnetism when current stops.

tf.questionText: Copper wire wrapped around a soft-iron core forms a common electromagnet.
tf.explanation: An electromagnet is made by winding insulated copper wire around a soft-iron core.

tf.questionText: A relay allows a small current to control a much larger current in a separate circuit.
tf.explanation: This is the main purpose of a relay, using an electromagnet to operate switch contacts.

tf.questionText: An electric motor converts electrical energy into chemical energy.
tf.explanation: An electric motor converts electrical energy into mechanical (rotational) energy.

tf.questionText: Electromagnetic induction can occur even if both the magnet and the coil are completely stationary.
tf.explanation: Induction requires a changing magnetic field, usually caused by relative movement between the magnet and the coil.

tf.questionText: A magnetic field line never crosses another magnetic field line.
tf.explanation: Magnetic field lines never cross because the field has only one direction at any point.

tf.questionText: A generator and a simple electric motor have a similar basic structure of a coil between magnets.
tf.explanation: Both use a coil rotating in a magnetic field; the motor uses current to produce motion, while the generator uses motion to produce current.

summary.correctAnswer: Like poles repel, unlike poles attract.
summary.explanation: This rule governs how two magnets interact when brought near each other.

summary.correctAnswer: The region around a magnet where a magnetic force is felt.
summary.explanation: It is represented by field lines running from north to south outside the magnet.

summary.correctAnswer: A current-carrying conductor produces a magnetic field around it.
summary.explanation: This was discovered by Oersted and is the basis of electromagnets.

summary.correctAnswer: A temporary magnet made by passing current through a coil around a soft-iron core.
summary.explanation: It is magnetic only while the current flows.

summary.correctAnswer: Current size, number of coil turns, and the use of a soft-iron core.
summary.explanation: Increasing current and turns and using a soft-iron core make it stronger.

summary.correctAnswer: Uses an electromagnet and a make-and-break circuit to vibrate a hammer against a gong.
summary.explanation: The repeated making and breaking of the circuit produces continuous ringing.

summary.correctAnswer: An electromagnetic switch that lets a small current control a larger circuit.
summary.explanation: It is used for safety and to control high-power circuits remotely.

summary.correctAnswer: A current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field experiences a force.
summary.explanation: This force is used to make electric motors turn.

summary.correctAnswer: A changing magnetic field through a coil induces a voltage and current.
summary.explanation: It is the principle on which generators work.

summary.correctAnswer: A motor changes electrical energy to motion; a generator changes motion to electricity.
summary.explanation: They are essentially reverse processes using a coil in a magnetic field.

hoq.questionText: A student builds two electromagnets using identical batteries and the same length of wire. Electromagnet X has 50 turns around a soft-iron nail, while electromagnet Y has 100 turns around an identical nail. Which statement is correct?

options.text: X is stronger because fewer turns concentrate the current
Y is stronger because more turns produce a stronger magnetic field
Both have exactly equal strength since the battery is the same
Neither is magnetic because soft iron cannot be magnetised

hoq.explanation: With the same current and core, the electromagnet with more turns produces a stronger magnetic field, so Y is stronger.

hoq.questionText: A bar magnet is pushed quickly into a coil connected to a galvanometer, then held still inside the coil. What happens to the galvanometer reading?

options.text: It shows a steady deflection the whole time
It deflects while the magnet moves, then returns to zero when held still
It shows no deflection at any time
It deflects only when the magnet is completely still

hoq.explanation: A current is induced only while the magnetic field through the coil is changing; once the magnet is held still, the field is constant and no current flows.

hoq.questionText: Why is a soft-iron core, rather than a steel core, preferred for the electromagnet used in an electric bell?

options.text: Steel cannot conduct electricity through the coil
Soft iron magnetises and demagnetises quickly, allowing rapid make-and-break action
Soft iron stays permanently magnetised so the bell rings forever
Steel is lighter and vibrates faster than soft iron

hoq.explanation: Soft iron loses its magnetism quickly when current stops, which is essential for the rapid switching of the armature that makes a bell ring continuously.
